analysis.title: Asia Equity Strategy: Market Dislocations and Risk Management
key_insights: Asian price action in recent months is dominated by flows and positioning shifts, with a very negative skew in reactions to earnings and newsflow (described as very late cycle). JPM attributes this to uncertainty over long-term fundamental outcomes in AI stocks, which is also driving non-AI stocks in inverse.

Last week's volatility after the US mid-term elections accelerated a drawdown in AI stocks, the Momentum factor, large-caps and Tech that had been under way since early October. JPM says the market read the election as lower Iran risk, greater fiscal discipline and constraints on data center buildout, and the last reading drove AI stocks lower.

AI stocks and Asian equity indices have broken below key technical levels, which JPM says threatens some knock-on volatility as market participants readjust. The market looks oversold and positioning has lightened, and JPM stays thematically bullish on AI.
JPM advises keeping a diversified portfolio for now: exposed to a potential sharp AI recovery (Figure 21) and to uncorrelated opportunities that benefit from easing macro risks (Figure 22).

Macro risks cited in JPM's September caution (Fed hiking cycle, higher long yields, JPY strength hitting carry trades, elevated oil, mid-term seasonality) are described as largely resolved. Fed pricing for end-2027 has stabilized, DM long-end yields and oil have moderated, and hyperscaler credit spreads have stabilized.

Asian equities are down about 15% on a rolling monthly basis, the second time this year, a level where the market has tended to bottom over the past two years. Market-wide 14-day RSIs are below 30 and Tech sector RSIs are in the early 20s.

The Asian Price Momentum factor has fallen 45% from its June highs, almost as large as the 1998-99 and 2009 drawdowns. The US shows a similar Momentum crash. JPM links larger and more frequent Momentum drawdowns to higher leverage at market-neutral institutions such as multi-strategy and quant funds.

Multi-strategy and tech-focused hedge funds have substantially lowered exposure per fund performance and JPM Prime book data, though quant funds have not. Macro funds, trend-following CTAs and retail have also been sellers.

JPM's aggregate Asia positioning indicator, an average of 15 metrics, is at the 8th percentile (below the 10th), which typically marks a market bottom. Remaining AI crowding looks non-institutional, with retail, HNWI and long-term real money likely heavily exposed.
Near-term buyers differ by market: corporates, long-only funds and pensions in Korea, hedge funds and ETFs in Taiwan, government-linked flows in China, and rebuilding retail leverage in India.

On AI, JPM sees the economics working at every layer of the stack, and JPM Tech analysts see no signs of cycle-end in inventories, lead times or capacity ramp-up. Financing concerns, especially at neo-clouds, escalated last month, but JPM argues rental rates have improved since October, funding needs should slow from 2028 and most datacenter participants have strong balance sheets.

On the Democratic 'Blue Sweep', JPM says state-level rule changes could limit upside to the capex curve. It argues tighter compute constraints could instead support pricing power and longer AI capex, or projects could use workarounds such as relocation or on-site power. JPM calls this an intra-cycle reset and is more bullish than what looks like cycle-end pricing.

SK Hynix on 2026-28 consensus estimates is said to generate free cash flow greater than its market cap. A near-term AI recovery is expected to be led by higher-beta names with larger drawdowns, such as Korea Tech and Figure 21 names outside the mega-caps.

Non-AI Asia is driven more by the inverse of AI performance than by individual merits, but easing macro risks help it. Investors are warming to China (fiscal stimulus, local AI story) and India (cyclical recovery, earnings, lower oil import bill), and Democratic leadership could help Healthcare and renewables.

Sectors with low or negative correlation to APAC IT and positive returns: Financials (China, Thailand, Australia), Healthcare (Japan, Australia), Energy (China, Australia, Thailand), Staples (Korea, Japan, Australia), Telecom (HK, Taiwan) and Utilities (China A, HK, Australia).
Asia ex-Japan trend-adjusted forward P/E is well below average and revision breadth remains positive, particularly in Tech. Weekly Bloomberg newsflow on an 'AI bubble' is already extremely elevated.

trade_ideas.description: Own higher-beta Asia AI names that sold off hardest (Korea Tech and the Figure 21 screen outside mega-caps) for a potential sharp recovery
trade_ideas.rationale: JPM expects any near-term AI recovery to be led by higher-beta names with larger drawdowns, and sees cycle-end pricing as too pessimistic.
trade_ideas.risk: Further volatility as participants readjust after the break below key technical levels, and AI financing concerns at neo-clouds.

trade_ideas.description: Hold a diversified mix that adds Asia 'AI hedge' sectors (Financials, Healthcare, Energy, Staples, Telecom, Utilities) alongside AI exposure, using the Figure 22 single stocks
trade_ideas.rationale: These sectors show low or negative correlation to APAC IT while still delivering positive returns, and benefit from easing macro risks.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees AI economics working at every layer of the stack, rental rates improved since October, funding needs slowing from 2028 as capex growth decelerates, and strong balance sheets for most datacenter participants. Positioning is at the 8th percentile and RSIs are oversold.
tension_points.bear_case: Financing concerns escalated last month, especially at neo-clouds. AI stocks and Asian indices broke key technical levels, and the Blue Sweep could limit upside to the capex curve. Price action has a very negative skew to newsflow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs of cycle-end in inventories, shortening lead times or a rapid capacity ramp-up, which JPM Tech analysts say are not currently visible.
